Look, this game is great fun. I have had a blast with it over the course of nearly 100 hours and im sure i will have many more to come but it is not without fault.

The premise is there, and its strong. The ability for creative exploration is immense and there is nothing like the sense of pride you get when building a large ship or base in survival with your friends. But for as long as its been in Alpha/Beta and while many things have been fixed, much still lies on the road ahead.

Countless hard to describe bugs in multiplayer, loading/saving issues and limits to what you can build can make it difficult to enjoy this game. Having to disconnect and recconect every 10 minutes takes you out of the otherwise awesome immersion. Singleplayer works of course, but for being such an open game centered around the coop experience i find it difficult to enjoy it alone. Difficulty drops very quickly if youre not under constant threat from PvP or consistent NPC attack, making the game feel less and less challenging.

It is not a perfect game and thats what you get with an early access title like this. Ambitious as it is, I am sure they will have a product soon enough.

In the end, if you like base building with friends and have a fair bit of patience with bugs, you will enjoy this game no doubt. Otherwise, perhaps give it another year or so.

This is easily one of my most favorite games of all time. I'm a huge sci-fi fan, and avidly play first-person shooters and Minecraft. The creativity and ingenuity of the community has no bounds, from extensive ship design to taking munitions past the in-game missile launchers. Play it, never leave it.

Space engineers is in early alpha so it can be frustrating at times.
It has limitless possibilities: tanks, ring worlds, Deathstars. You name it you can build it here.
And Keen updates it WEEKLY with new content and bug fixes.
However I would recommend this to players with only higher end machines at least for now.
The game still has a long way to go as far as optimization.
But personally I think the game is fantastic and has great potential.
If you want to get into a alpha game, build your favorite ship from your favorite sci-fi series and just except the bugs and help shape the game in the forums this game is for you.
If you cant stand sub 40 FPS, CTD every third launch and a somewhat lack of content, stay away for about a year or two…

The first thing anyone should learn about playing Space Engineers is to never, ever get attached to your creations. They will explode, and it will happen because of something stupid (most likely caused by you).

After reaching a state of non-materialistic zen, though, Space Engineers is a great game with tons of possibilities. The mods available allow crazy amounts of customization if you're willing to put in the work. Creative mode with friends is fantastic for just messing around and blowing stuff up.

A quick glace at the game and it seems like a simple space sandbox, a run of the mill, buy once, cry once game that you imagine is lacking multiplayer capibillities, but if this is your takeaway, you are simply a fool.

This game has more or less given me a new lease on the sandbox genre with its handcrafted voxel mechanics, hyper-realistic physics, immaculate collision. The masterpiece of Keen Software. The Multiplayer scene is something else. Huge factions to be made with your freinds, warship battle, etc.

Get this game, starships were meant to fly.

Recommended. 8/10

I have a love/hate relationship with this game. Love the creativity and building. I don't love the lack of objectives and some bugs.

Pros:

- Unlimited creativity. I love building new ships and stations. This is the main reason I have so many hours.
- Many different kinds of blocks to add functionality and creative design to your builds.
- Much improved over the years. Many of the bugs that plagued the game early on have been eliminated.
- Great visuals.

Cons:

- Even though I purchased the DLC, I have never liked having additional paid content for games. But, to be fair, I have gotten over 2000 hours of entertainment out of a $20 dollar purchase. So I guess I shouldn't complain about spending an extra $20 on :).
- No objectives once you have built your base. Why are we building things except to have a cool ship?
- Some bugs still exist.

Like all good devs who get too big, they eventually go bad. Supported Space Engineers almost from the start, love it. Played it for hundreds of hours with friends. Keen would release meaningful updates weekly which we all looked forward to. We all bought Medieval Engineers as soon as it dropped based on Keen's previous reputation alone.

Fast forward to today. Medieval Engineers got pumped and dumped as abandonware. Keen throws out more DLC that would put paradox to shame. At least when Paradox does it they remember to include meaningful gameplay features. Been waiting for planet weather for years now, putting it down as my most wanted feature on surveys Keen emailed or posted online. Now its scenario only on one planet behind paywall. Is this all they have been working on for the past year? Is this why they scrapped ME to focus efforts on SE?

Keen Software Houses reputation might as well be on par with big names like Blizzard.
This game is for a certain niche of players. It combines trial and error, space, combat, industry, and minecraft into one conglomerate of a wonderful game. Beautiful.

Like Minecraft in space... With rockets!... and missiles... and all with the easy to use workshop for all your modding needs, no more sifting through folders to sort out conflicts etc =D

EDITED: Now out of early access, a few DLC to choose from which add visual options, along with more free additions that are released with functional blocks, mods keep getting better and more innovative (look at WeaponCore), and it also revived my passion for coding while attempting to make mods myself.

TLDR; anything you dont like you can change with mods, give it a go

After two years of owning this game, its come to my attention that, with all of my dearest heart, soul, and mind, I absolutely adore this game beyond anything I have ever known. If the game's mechanics that allow you to do just about anything are within your grasp, the possibilities of what you can slap together or meticulously craft are left to your wildest or most organized imaginations. The sequences that you can set up in a single Timer Block can be infinitely complex, or as simple as a door opening. Don't like the way that your fighter is put together? Well, redesign it however you'd like. Feel that the vanilla game is boring? Choose from hundreds and hundreds of mods and scripts from the constantly active and busy Workshop!!! Don't want to get mods? Get a DLC from the collection Keen Softwarehouse has already pubished and add some flavor to your game!!! Want in a server? BAM!! A server!!!!! Whatever you want to make, this game will let you make it, unless of course your creation is so massive and so complex that your computer is trying to murder itself by using the mystical ways of Lord Clang, then yeah, don't make it bro...

Space Engineers has been a staple in my Steam library for a long time now. While I got my start in creative and didn't think much of attempting survival, the absolute scale of this game really shows itself when you take a stab at learning the progression from square one. Every step of the journey, every successful mechanism you create feels like a massive achievement, because -you- design your own road to success (whatever that image of success is for you). The team at Keen have lovingly continued to add to Space Engineers in real tangible ways that bring new experiences and stories with each update! I'm 500 hours in, and I know I'll be playing Space Engineers for many many more.
I realy enjoy this game. I played a 100 hrs alone and it was fun. Now I am playing with a friend and the time went by even feaster. It has a fewe kinks, but I still recommend it.

As much is i try to love the game, the UI and controls are just way to clunky, it is plagued with bugs like symmetry mode just not working properly, sometimes the blocks on the mirrored side just don't connect or don't even appear.
And the game has got weird limits like a 110 m/s speed limit on EVERYTHING in a SPACE game. Sure there are mods that disable that limit, but don't expect the game to be stable if you do. According to the devs speed bugs are their game engine's fault and cannot be fixed.
Don't expect this to be a "Minecraft in space" level of quality. This should still be in early access.

tldr.text: Very Positive (89%): players praise the mods and customization options.
The main complaint is bugs and crashes, with lag and connection problems on the servers.

details.text: Recent reviews are slightly less positive, at 83%, than the all-time score.
Players with little time logged are far less positive than veterans, at 59%, and one reviewer said it is "challenging to wrap your head around the controls at first".
